Stage 1 audio/Crow work merged at f301e76. Review stage 2 only: sampler/softcut services, real audio file errors, generic media imports and configurable native input timeout, explicit Crow absence, native virtual arc and browser integration. Audio implementation is explicitly authorized. Desktop/Maiden/Docker are deferred.
# Broader-script combined candidate

Stage 1 is merged at `f301e76`. This stage remains in `codex/audio-monitor`,
pending the bounded review and admission. The default installation, user demo,
external applications and concurrent main state are preserved.

Candidate `.runtime/arc-tools-01/installation.json` composes the fresh canonical

content.text:
## What works

- `patches/norns/experimental-softcut-read-bounds.patch:8–9` adds `"clamp(frDur, ... - frSrc)"` and `"clamp(frDur, bufFrames - frDst)"`. These match the surrounding read-to-end bounds and preserve existing mixing behavior. Retained baseline/candidate sentinel results show four failures becoming four passes.
- `scripts/arc_native_patch.py:53` uses `"event_data_new(EVENT_ARC_ENCODER_DELTA)"`. Arc input reaches the existing native/Lua handlers; LED behavior remains upstream-owned.
- `src/runtime/audio_files.py:30–35` uses `"target.open('xb')"` and `"original.read(1024*1024)"`. Imports avoid overwriting destinations and hash the bytes actually copied.
- `tests/cheat_codes_record.py:21` selects `"frequency=600"` without weakening the shared signal or xrun gates. Its integer-cycle rationale is sound for the documented loop; the retained 660 Hz failure remains visible, and arbitrary-loop continuity is explicitly excluded. This agrees with the [coherent-sampling principle](https://www.analog.com/en/resources/technical-articles/coherent-sampling-vs-window-sampling.html).

## What doesn't work

- [MAJOR] **A timed-out arc transition leaves a healthy session with incorrect input state.** `src/runtime/native.py:452–453` executes `"self.send(...)"` before `"self.arc_input.applied(action)"`, while line 385 merely raises `"native_ack_timeout"`. If a key-down callback finishes after that deadline, native state changes but neither held-input bookkeeping nor ownership is committed; subsequent observations can report healthy with no held key, explicit key-up rejects as a duplicate transition, and `release_all` misses it. The retained `artifacts/audio/slow-input-20260908-191822/2/native-events.jsonl:140–142` already demonstrates the underlying late-completion behavior: timeout, then completion MIDI and acknowledgement. This contradicts the intent to preserve input ownership and explicit errors.

- [MAJOR] **The HTTP deadline covers one native callback, but disconnect/release can execute several.** `src/automation/session.py:21` budgets `"max(5,info.get('input_timeout',2)+3)"`; `src/runtime/native.py:449` releases each held arc key through a separate `"self.query(...)"`, each receiving a fresh native timeout. With `input_timeout=8` and three held keys whose release callbacks take 5.2 seconds each, disconnect exceeds the Python client’s 11-second deadline despite every callback meeting its configured bound; the server continues applying the action after the client fails, losing acknowledgement/sequence synchronization. Browser fetch waits through the same operation, contradicting the claimed browser/automation parity.

## Risks

- [MAJOR] **An allowed long callback can expire an actively connected browser’s lease.** `src/automation/server.py:220` holds `"app.lock"` throughout native execution; heartbeat handling also needs that lock, while line 100 expires clients when `"time.monotonic()-last>self.client_timeout"` and line 44 fixes that timeout at 2.5 seconds. After a successful 5.2-second callback, if the waiting watchdog acquires the lock before queued heartbeats, it releases the browser’s held inputs and closes its audio monitor. The new slow-input test has no browser owner, so it does not exercise this race.

## Gaps

Nothing notable beyond the missing regression cases identified above.

## Improvements

- [MAJOR] At `src/runtime/native.py:385`, make `"native_ack_timeout"` a sticky session failure unless late completion is explicitly reconciled. Cost: a small failure-state change and a native regression checking post-timeout health, release behavior and teardown.
- [MAJOR] Replace the independently renewed deadlines behind `src/runtime/native.py:449` and `src/automation/session.py:21` with a consistent action-level deadline. Cost: deadline propagation through compound releases and one multi-held-input regression.
- [MAJOR] Prevent server-blocked heartbeat processing from counting as browser inactivity at `src/automation/server.py:100`. Cost: lease-accounting adjustment plus a browser test that holds input across an allowed slow callback and verifies subsequent genuine disconnect cleanup.
